sections.heading: Relations, Functions & Equivalence Counting
sections.summary: On set A of size n, total relations = 2^(n^2), reflexive = 2^(n^2 - n), symmetric = 2^(n(n+1)/2), equivalence relations = Bell number B_n.
keyPoints: Function checks: Vertical line cuts at most once; One-One (Injective): Horizontal line cuts at most once, or f'(x) >= 0 / <= 0 strictly.
Onto (Surjective) from m elements to n elements: Sum_{k=0}^n (-1)^k C(n,k) (n-k)^m. For A(n)->A(n), injective <=> bijective!
Periodicity: sin^n(x), cos^n(x) have period pi (n even), 2*pi (n odd); |sin x| + |cos x| has period pi/2; {x} (fractional part) has period 1; constant functions have NO fundamental period.

sections.heading: Inverse Trigonometric Functions & Principal Branches
sections.summary: Restrict trigonometric domains cleanly so inverses stay single-valued and continuous.
keyPoints: Principal ranges: sin^(-1), tan^(-1), cosec^(-1) in [-pi/2, pi/2]; cos^(-1), cot^(-1), sec^(-1) in [0, pi].
Always enforce complementary pairs: sin^(-1)x + cos^(-1)x = pi/2 (|x| <= 1); tan^(-1)x + cot^(-1)x = pi/2 (all real x).
Sum addition trap: tan^(-1)x + tan^(-1)y = tan^(-1)((x+y)/(1-xy)) ONLY when xy < 1; add +pi if x>0, y>0, xy > 1!

formulas.formula: sin^(-1)(sin x) = x [-pi/2, pi/2] ; pi - x [pi/2, 3pi/2]
formulas.note: Period = 2*pi sawtooth wave peaking at +pi/2 and -pi/2
Applies whenever x > 0, y > 0 and x*y > 1
Standard continuous polynomial/power function signatures

traps: Forgetting +pi correction in tan^(-1)(2) + tan^(-1)(3) gives acute value instead of 3*pi/4!
If f(x) + f(1/x) = f(x)f(1/x) for polynomial f, then f(x) = 1 +/- x^n.

sections.heading: Matrices, Special Types & Adjoint Identities
sections.summary: Every square matrix A splits uniquely into Symmetric (A + A^T)/2 plus Skew-Symmetric (A - A^T)/2.
keyPoints: Skew-symmetric odd order matrix MUST have det(A) = 0; main diagonal entries are ALL zero.
Adjoint golden laws (for n x n non-singular A, |A| != 0): A (adj A) = |A| I; |adj A| = |A|^(n-1); adj(adj A) = |A|^(n-2) A; |adj(adj A)| = |A|^((n-1)^2).
(AB)^(-1) = B^(-1) A^(-1); (AB)^T = B^T A^T (sock-and-shoe reversal!). Orthogonal matrix A^T A = I => |A| = +/- 1.

sections.heading: Determinants & Consistency of Linear Systems AX = B
sections.summary: Cramer's determinants Delta, Delta_1, Delta_2, Delta_3 classify unique, infinite, and zero solutions cleanly.
keyPoints: Non-homogeneous AX = B: Delta != 0 => Unique solution (Consistent). Delta = 0 and any Delta_i != 0 => No solution (Inconsistent).
Delta = 0 and ALL Delta_i = 0 => Infinitely many (or parallel planes exception — check rank / elimination of variables directly!).
Homogeneous AX = 0: always consistent (trivial 0,0,0). Non-trivial solution exists iff Delta = 0.

formulas.formula: |k A| = k^n |A| (for n x n matrix)
formulas.note: k factors out from EACH of the n rows individually

traps: Delta = 0 with Delta_x = Delta_y = Delta_z = 0 CAN STILL be inconsistent if two equations represent parallel planes (e.g. x+y+z=1 and x+y+z=2)! Always verify rank directly!
|A + B| != |A| + |B| in general! Never split determinants additively row-wide without identical rows.

sections.heading: Argand Rotation Theorem (Coni Method) & nth Roots of Unity

sections.heading: Cayley-Hamilton Theorem & High Matrix Powers
sections.summary: Every n x n square matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial equation p(lambda) = det(A - lambda I) = 0.

For 3x3 matrix A: A^3 - tr(A) A^2 + [Sum minor_ii] A - det(A) I = 0.
Matrix trace identity: Sum of eigenvalues = tr(A); Product of eigenvalues = det(A).
